texts.facts: The petitioners have challenged the correctness of an order dated 09.01.2026 passed by the Karnataka State Administrative Tribunal (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for short) at Kalaburagi in Application Nos.20902 and 20903/2025. The petitioners contend that they had challenged the order of their repatriation before the Tribunal and that the Tribunal heard the petitioners on the interim prayer but reserved the case for orders on the main application itself on 19.12.2025, and disposed of the applications on 09.01.2026. The petitioners contend that they were not heard on the merits of the applications and that they were heard only on the interim reliefs.
texts.arguments: 2. The learned counsel for the petitioners reiterated the above and invited the attention of the Court to the order sheet of the Tribunal and contended that the Tribunal took up the applications for consideration of the interim prayer on 19.12.2025 and reserved the case. He NC: 2026:KHC-K:407-DB HC-KAR contends that the petitioners were not heard on the merits of the applications and, therefore, the order dated 09.01.2026 passed by the Tribunal disposing of the applications is without hearing the petitioners. 3. The learned Additional Government Advocate for the respondents, after perusing the order sheet maintained by the Tribunal, did not dispute the fact that the case was listed before the Tribunal on 19.12.2025 and that the petitioners were heard only on the interim prayer and not on the merits of the case.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 2. The learned Additional Government Advocate for the respondents, after perusing the order sheet maintained by the Tribunal, did not dispute the fact that the case was listed before the Tribunal on 19.12.2025 and that the petitioners were heard only on the interim prayer and not on the merits of the case.
